requirements.title: Findings Knowledge Store — SQLite Schema, CRUD, and Semantic Index
requirements.description: Own a SQLite database (using api-core storage utilities) that stores two entity types: (1) Finding — atomic unit comprising a cited claim, source citations (URLs + titles), retrieval date, confidence score [0,1], status (active/disputed/superseded), originating brief ID, and audit metadata; (2) Brief — research run container holding many findings plus provenance (query, run timestamp, agent/user, L3 run ID). Semantic indexing of findings is provided via aisearch-go (nomic embeddings via Qdrant) enabling semantic recall. No writes into knowledge-observatory.

validation.notes: Finding schema validation: a finding row with missing required fields (claim, source_citations, retrieval_date) fails insertion with a descriptive error
Finding confidence field accepts only values in [0,1] and rejects out-of-range values
Finding status field accepts only the enum values {active, disputed, superseded} and rejects unknown values
Brief schema validation: a brief row requires query and run_timestamp fields
CRUD: create, read, update (edit fields), and soft-delete (supersede) operations each return the expected state on round-trip
Audit metadata (mutated_by, mutation_reason, source_brief_id) is written on every finding mutation
Write a finding, trigger aisearch-go reindex, issue a semantic query, and verify the finding is recalled in the top-N results
Verify that findings data is stored in the web-search-owned SQLite database and no writes occur in the knowledge-observatory store
aisearch-go Source/Service pattern mirrors cli-health integration pattern — verify registration and index-refresh lifecycle
Semantic recall query over a 10,000-finding index returns top-10 results within 300ms at p95
A research finding ingested from an L3 run is retrievable via both exact ID lookup and semantic similarity query
Every finding carries full provenance (source URLs, retrieval date, originating brief) enabling human auditability
